text: The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, and equipment to de-install, remove, and dispose of the specified GE INNOVA 4100-IQ systems in accordance with OEM specifications, safety, and infection control requirements, and provide all required documentation and reports to the COR.

citations.quote: The contractor shall furnish all labor, tools, materials, equipment, and transportation necessary to fully de-install, remove, transport, and dispose of two (2) GE INNOVA 4100-IQ imaging systems and associated peripheral subcomponents from Radiology (1D44/1D42A in building 1) at the George E Wahlen Veterans Affairs Medical Center, Salt Lake City UT.
Work shall be performed in accordance with Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specifications and all applicable VA, federal, state, and local requirements.
The contractor shall:
Provide all personnel, supervision, tools, materials, equipment, and transportation required to complete the work described in this PWS.
The contractor shall:
Perform all tasks in accordance with OEM specifications, applicable codes, VA policies, and infection control requirements.
The contractor shall:
Coordinate all on-site activities with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) to minimize disruption to patient care and hospital operations.
Perform necessary diagnostic checks and visual inspection of both GE INNOVA 4100-IQ systems and related subcomponents to identify any issues that may impact safe removal.
Confirm all utilities (e.g., power, data, grounding) are safely isolated or otherwise controlled in accordance with facility procedures prior to disassembly.

Establish and maintain an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) Level IV compliant work area surrounding the Radiology room, including dust barriers and any required protective measures as directed by the facility Infection Prevention and/or Safety offices.
Implement appropriate debris control, cleaning, and containment measures throughout de-installation and removal activities.
Disassemble the GE INNOVA 4100-IQ imaging systems and its peripheral subcomponents in accordance with OEM specifications and good engineering practices.
Protect adjacent walls, floors, ceilings, and installed clinical equipment from damage during removal.
Remove all disassembled components from the Radiology room and transport them out of the facility using routes approved by the COR.
Load and secure all components for off-site transport in a safe and compliant manner.

Dispose of all removed components in accordance with all applicable federal, state, local, and VA regulations and policies, including those governing electronic waste, metal scrap, and any hazardous materials, if present.
Provide documentation, if requested by the COR, verifying proper disposal (e.g., disposal receipt, recycling certificate).
Remove all anchoring bolts or similar hardware from the floor related to the GE INNOVA 4100-IQ systems installation.
Restore the floor surface to a “flush” condition (e.g., filling or covering bolt holes) suitable for subsequent construction or installation activities as directed by the COR.
Remove all trash and debris generated by the removal activities and leave the area clean and free of dust and debris.
At the direction of the COR or Contracting Officer (CO), the contractor shall instead:

Disassemble and remove the ceiling-mounted monitor arm and monitor in accordance with OEM specifications and facility safety requirements; transport and dispose of them as part of the overall system disposal scope.
At the direction of the COR or Contracting Officer (CO), the contractor shall instead:

Disengage the ceiling-mounted monitor arm and monitor from the GE INNOVA 4100-IQ systems as needed while maintaining them safely in place, ensuring they are left in a secure, stable, and usable condition (or in a condition as directed by the COR).
The contractor shall be prepared to execute either option as directed by the COR prior to or during field operations.
The contractor shall provide the following deliverables to the COR:
Confirmation (verbal and noted on the service report) that an ICRA Level IV compliant area was established and maintained for the duration of work.
A detailed field service report upon completion of work, including at a minimum:
Equipment identification (e.g., device name, model, serial number, VA EE number if applicable).
A detailed field service report upon completion of work, including at a minimum:
Date(s) and time(s) on site.
A detailed field service report upon completion of work, including at a minimum:
Description of tasks performed (disassembly, removal, transport, disposal, floor restoration, clean-up, etc.).
A detailed field service report upon completion of work, including at a minimum:
Confirmation of whether the ceiling-mounted monitor arm and monitor were removed or retained and their final disposition.
A detailed field service report upon completion of work, including at a minimum:
Any issues encountered and corrective actions taken.
The report shall be submitted to Biomedical Engineering and the COR.
Documentation evidencing compliant disposal of equipment (e.g., manifests, certificates) when requested by the COR.
The contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, local, and VA safety requirements, including but not limited to OSHA regulations and facility safety policies.
The contractor shall implement and maintain an ICRA Level IV work area as described in Section 3.2, including dust control, barrier installation, and housekeeping.
At the direction of the facility, the contractor shall immediately correct any identified safety issues.
Remove and dispose of all equipment associated with the two GE INNOVA 4100-IQ imaging systems (Serial Numbers: 589832BU5 and 436339BU6, EEs: 57204 and 40402) in a timely fashion.
Communicate with COR about progress in a timely fashion
Maintain ICRA Level IV compliant work area
Remove all anchoring bolts/other hardware and restore floor to a “flush” condition suitable for future construction
100% removal of all trash and debris
Submission of field service report and disposal documentation.

text: All Field Service Engineers (FSEs) must be fully qualified, having completed formal OEM training and possessing at least two years of relevant field experience; documentation of these qualifications must be provided upon request.

citations.quote: All Field Service Engineers (FSEs) performing work under this PWS shall be fully qualified and authorized by the contractor to perform de-installation and removal of the GE INNOVA 4100-IQ systems or similar imaging systems.
“Fully qualified” FSEs shall:
Have successfully completed formal OEM or equivalent training for imaging system de-installation and related tasks
“Fully qualified” FSEs shall:
Have at least two (2) years of field experience with scheduled and unscheduled maintenance or de-installation of comparable imaging systems (except for equipment newly introduced to the market).
Documentation of training and qualifications shall be provided to the COR upon request.

text: The offeror must certify compliance with limitations on subcontracting (not exceeding 50% for services) and acknowledges that this certification is subject to federal oversight and potential penalties for fraud.

citations.quote: ) Pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 8127(l)(2), the offeror certifies that
If awarded a contract (see FAR 2.101 definition), it will comply with the limitations on subcontracting requirement as provided in the solicitation and the resultant contract

In the case of a contract for services (except construction), the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-73 or certified VOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219-74.
Any work that a similarly situated certified SDVOSB/VOSB subcontractor further subcontracts will count towards the 50% subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.
The offeror acknowledges that this certification concerns a matter within the jurisdiction of an Agency of the United States.

The offeror further acknowledges that this certification is subject to Title 18, United States Code, Section 1001, and, as such, a false, fictitious, or fraudulent certification may render the offeror subject to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties, including prosecution.

The offeror represents and understands that by submission of its offer and award of a contract it may be required to provide copies of documents or records to VA that VA may review to determine whether the offeror complied with the limitations on subcontracting requirement specified in the contract.
